title: Kushan Empire
summary: The Kushan empire ruled Bactria, Gandhara and northern India from the first to the mid-third century CE, contending with Parthia as a major power. Kanishka is linked to Peshawar and Mathura. Its position between Central and South Asia boosted Silk Road trade and the spread of Buddhism. Dating of the Kanishka era is debated.

uncertainty.note: Century-level dates only: start is somewhere in the first century CE; the last Kushans continue to about 250-300 CE per the UW essay. The start of the Kaniska era is unresolved (78 CE traditional versus about 100 CE).

as_recorded.value: During the first to mid-third centuries CE, the empire of the Kushans
the Kushan period in the first to third centuries CE

where.modern_name: Peshawar, Pakistan (city especially associated with Kanishka; the realm spanned Bactria to the Ganges valley)
where.historical_name: Peshawar, in the Kushan realm (Bactria, Gandhara, northern India)

importance.justification: A major imperial power linking Central and South Asia, central to Silk Road trade and the transmission of Buddhism.

reviewer_note: Dates are century-level; the pin is Peshawar only as a symbolic centre of a realm that also centred on Bactria and Mathura (the UW essay names no single capital). The Kanishka era start is unresolved, so no dated reign is claimed. Founder and capital names were not confirmed on opened pages and are not stated.
